## ⚠️ A path correction this seat owes you, made while verifying

The card and the comment both cite the pin by **bare filename**, which is how the comment spells it too. This seat first looked for it under `packages/core/src/security/` — **it is not there**. Measured location:

⇒ ⛔ The card is **not** wrong; this seat's directory assumption was, and it is recorded so you do not lose ten minutes to the same guess.

## ⛔ That file is in ANOTHER LANE. Read it; do not edit it.

`packages/plugins/plugin-security/**` is `domain:services` by the lane table. It is **outside your file surface** and outside this lane.

- ✅ **Read it** — you must, to state what the pin actually records now.
- ⛔ **Do not edit it**, even if its own superseded-quotation block also reads oddly. If you conclude it needs a change, **report that**; a follow-up card in the owning lane is this seat's to file, ⛔ not yours to ride in on this PR.

⭐ Note the shape you are repairing, because it is subtle: the pin's string survives as an **explicitly-superseded quotation** inside a block marked 「RE-AUTHORED by #16682」. So the comment's citation resolves to text that now says the **opposite** of what the comment claims it says. ⇒ 「the citation still resolves」 and 「the citation supports the claim」 are two different questions, and only the first is true.

## R3 was acted on, not merely acknowledged

The dispatch's whole point was that 「the citation **resolves**」 and 「the citation **supports the claim**」 are different questions. The dev read the pin at source and established what it records **now**: the string survives only inside the `:434-456` block marked 「RE-AUTHORED by #16682」, which quotes the maintainer ruling and is followed by the case 「a declared owner **DOES** redirect the single-org promotion」.

⇒ The comment is re-keyed to post-ruling behaviour **and the citation re-pointed at what the pin actually records**, ⛔ not merely stripped of the false sentence. The gate's justification is restated from what the reversal did **not** change — the declared-owner leg mints the same unscoped row through the single `promote()` call site, and a rig already holding one returns `already_have_admin` before that leg runs.

## ⭐ The neighbouring clause WAS also stale — the half-fix warning paid for itself

The dispatch said: 「check whether that framing is still accurate before you leave it standing … a comment repaired in one clause and left stale in the next is a half-fix」.

It was stale. Per #11663 comment `5404675670`, **Choice 4B is 「ruled as the sequenced follow-up, not dropped」** — so 「whichever way 4B is eventually ruled」 was itself false, and is now 「ruled and filed, not landed」.

⇒ ⭐ One card repaired **two** stale claims because the order asked for the sweep rather than the named line. That is the difference between fixing a defect and fixing a comment.

## ⭐ The changeset question was MEASURED, and the result generalises

`@objectstack/core` ships `['dist','README.md','CHANGELOG.md']`. After building:

| needle | hits in published paths |
|:--|:--|
| text from this comment | **0** |
| a second needle from a pre-existing **body** comment in the same function | **0** |
| ⭐ positive control — a **docblock on the exported** `hasPlatformAdminStanding` | **1** in `dist/index.d.ts`, **1** in `dist/index.d.cts` |

⇒ **A function-BODY comment reaches no published artifact** — the declaration emitter carries declaration-level docblocks only, esbuild drops body comments, and `dropSourcesContent` keeps source text out of the map. Control lands, needles do not.

⭐⭐ **This is the third data point in one round on 「does a comment ship」**, and together they form a usable rule: a **docblock on an exported symbol** ships (#18331, measured in the real tarball); a **detached docblock sitting above** an exported symbol **also** ships, because the dts bundler emits both blocks (#18331); a **function-body comment does not** (this card). ⇒ Future cards in this family can decide the changeset question from where the comment sits, and then verify rather than explore.

## Deviations — accepted, and one is a third data point of its own

- ⚠️ **Report field set**: the dispatch named nine machine-checkable fields; the role file mandates a different set. The dev reported the **UNION** and flagged it rather than silently picking a side. ⭐ Correct — and this is the **third** dev this round to flag a divergence between this seat's orders and `os-dev.md` (the earlier two were the write budget). ⇒ One is an oversight, three is a pattern: **this seat's orders have been quietly narrowing or restating role-file clauses.** Recorded on the seat post (`5713135981`); orders now defer to the role file explicitly.
- ⭐ **Commit trailer**: the model-free `Claude` spelling was used and the pre-push gate confirmed it. The dispatch's up-front warning saved the bounce every earlier dev paid.
- Two `NOT MEASURED` families (exit 3, whole-repo dist prerequisite), declared to CI. The known `check:cross-package-test-inputs` red was named with a **control measured in place** — with `packages/spec/dist` moved aside the same command exits 0, restored afterwards at 216 files before and after. ⛔ Not chased, ⛔ not twinned.
- Repo-wide `pnpm lint` run in **full**, so ⛔ no narrowing had to be declared.

## Findings

⏹️ The `describe` title in the plugin-security pin still reads 「…UNCHANGED (Choice 4A)」 while the case inside asserts the redirect. Correctly **noted, not filed**: the block's own re-authored docblock states the split correctly, so it is a title-level nit a reader cannot copy into failure, and the file is `domain:services` — **read-only for this card, per the claim, and the dev respected that.** ⭐ Its named successor is #11979's implementer, who rewrites that block when Choice 4B lands.
